solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Singer’s sad attempt to pick up start of recitative

indicators.note: to pick something up is to take it inside, so one piece gets enclosed by another
the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one letter is kept

blocks.note: feeling blue is feeling sad
a bid is an attempt at something
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A vocalist makes a sorry attempt to launch into the sung speech of an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer’s' reads as a possessive, but the apostrophe-s is just 'is'; the singer is a bird, not an opera star.
explanation.definitionFit: The bluebird is a small songbird of North America, so calling it a singer is fair.

clue.text: Cut of beef, one almost entirely fit for a nobleman

indicators.note: almost the whole thing means stopping one letter short, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a baron of beef is a large joint of two sirloins joined at the backbone
the Roman numeral for one
entirely means all of it

explanation.surface: A joint of beef that one could almost serve to a lord.
explanation.walkthrough: A baron of beef is a big traditional British roast; ALL loses its last letter to become AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Baronial describes things belonging to or suited to a baron, a titled member of the peerage.

clue.text: University acceptable for workers’ group

blocks.note: the everyday short form of university
as in 'that's just not on', meaning not acceptable

explanation.surface: A university deemed suitable for a trade body to use.
explanation.walkthrough: Acceptable is usually U in crosswords; here it is ON, from the idiom 'it's not on'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade union is an organised association of employees formed to protect their pay and conditions.

clue.text: Composer’s predicament in African state — and his own, we hear

indicators.note: one thing placed within another sits inside it
what we hear is the sound of a word rather than its spelling

blocks.note: Benin is a country in West Africa
being in a jam is being in a predicament
his own state is his home country, Britain

explanation.surface: A composer caught in a tight spot in an African country, and in his homeland too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his own' state, set against the African one, is his home country, Britain, which sounds like the composer's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Britten was the twentieth-century English composer of Peter Grimes and the War Requiem.

clue.text: Consider others, concealing muscle

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it inside, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: the rest means the others
short for pectoral, a chest muscle

explanation.surface: An instruction to be thoughtful of other people while hiding one's strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consider others' reads as one phrase about being considerate; the definition is only the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: To respect someone's wishes is to have regard for them, to take them into account.

clue.text: Hare-brained sort initially apt to make spiteful remarks

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of a word

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
a catty person makes spiteful, sly remarks

explanation.surface: A foolish type who is at first inclined to be nasty about people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' looks like the link, but it belongs to the description of CATTY; the definition is the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatty is British informal for scatterbrained, disorganised and absent-minded, just like hare-brained.

clue.text: See beautiful girls cutting last of ornate flowers

indicators.note: cutting something removes a part of it
the last of a word is its closing letter

blocks.note: a see is a bishop's seat; Canterbury is the Archbishop's
belles are beautiful young women
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Look at pretty girls trimming the fancy blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' reads as a verb, but it is the noun: a diocese. Take E out of BELLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Canterbury bells are a garden campanula with large bell-shaped blooms, so they are plants in flower.

clue.text: Neat, adopting Indonesian island’s loyalty to race

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: trim means neat and tidy
Bali is an Indonesian island, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A tidy person taking up an island's devotion to its own people.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is kept as a letter S, attached to the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribalism is strong allegiance to one's own ethnic group or tribe above others.

clue.text: Servile types principally seen in Arabian republic

indicators.note: principally means first of all, so the opening letter
one thing placed within another sits inside it

blocks.note: Yemen is a republic on the Arabian peninsula
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Obsequious people are mostly to be found in a Middle Eastern country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principally seen' reads as 'mainly found', but it only supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes men are sycophants who always agree with their superiors, the very picture of servility.

clue.text: English thriller writer left in shade?

indicators.note: one thing placed within another sits inside it

blocks.note: amber is a shade of yellowish orange
the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A crime novelist left in the dark, or perhaps in the shadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shade' suggests shadow; it is a colour. The question mark flags the unexpected sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Ambler was an English novelist famed for spy fiction such as The Mask of Dimitrios.

clue.text: Give up work, releasing son to hold sway

indicators.note: releasing something lets it go, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: to resign is to give up one's job
the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone quits their job and lets their boy take over.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S from RESIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule as monarch, to have power and authority over others.

clue.text: Jerks following celebrities reflected meaningful study?

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front
following means coming after, so this piece is placed second

blocks.note: big names are celebrities
tics are involuntary twitches or jerks

explanation.surface: Idiots copying famous people considered a deep piece of research.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerks' suggests fools, but they are twitches. The question mark marks the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Semantics is the branch of linguistics concerned with meaning, so it is literally the study of meaning.

clue.text: Nothing absorbing on skin is unique

indicators.note: to absorb is to take in, so other letters are taken inside

blocks.note: nil means nothing
taken as written
to pare is to peel or skin

explanation.surface: A skincare claim: nothing soaks into the skin quite like this one-of-a-kind cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skin' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to peel.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonpareil means having no equal, unrivalled, so it matches an adjective for something one of a kind.

clue.text: Dodge eastern fellow going west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means running right to left, backwards

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for eastern
any man's name can stand for a fellow

explanation.surface: An oriental man heads west to avoid something.
explanation.walkthrough: E and DAVE together run backwards; the east-west contrast in the surface is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge a question or duty is to avoid it cleverly, which is what evading means.

clue.text: Emergency flight served by express elevator

blocks.note: to air a view is to express it
lift is the British word for an elevator

explanation.surface: A rapid-transit elevator gets people out fast in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'express elevator' reads as one phrase, a fast lift; split it, and 'express' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An airlift transports supplies or people by aircraft, especially in a crisis where roads are blocked.

clue.text: Strengthen army corps having legal validity

blocks.note: the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a law in force is valid and binding

explanation.surface: Beefing up a military unit with lawful authority.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a standard army abbreviation; 'in force' is the legal phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce a wall or an army is to make it stronger by adding support.

clue.text: Religious teacher given time to chatter

blocks.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher
the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A cleric is allowed a moment to have a gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit on is British slang for talking at length, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' for talk.
explanation.definitionFit: In British informal speech, to rabbit is to talk endlessly about trivial things.

clue.text: Move forward, carrying large club

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it inside

blocks.note: to budge on is to shift further along
the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Advancing while holding a heavy weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large club' looks like one noun phrase; 'large' is only a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bludgeon is a thick heavy stick used as a weapon, which is one kind of club.

clue.text: Quick bite bishops demanded in middle of river

indicators.note: being required to sit in the middle of something means going inside it

blocks.note: the Nile is the great African river
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Clergy insist on a snack halfway across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: BB goes right in the middle of NILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nibble is a small quick mouthful, a light snack taken in little bites.

clue.text: Junior officer’s quarters good for stopping crime

indicators.note: stopping a hole means plugging it, sitting inside the gap

blocks.note: E and N are two of the four compass points, or quarters
a sin is a wrongdoing
the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A young officer's lodgings are good at preventing lawbreaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' suggests lodgings; here it means compass points, of which two are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is the lowest commissioned rank in some navies, and historically in infantry regiments.

clue.text: Chewy sweet painter fed to artiodactyl mammal

indicators.note: food fed to an animal goes inside it

blocks.note: camels are even-toed ungulates, artiodactyls
a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A toffee given to a camel by an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is the standard crossword painter; the long word for 'even-toed' is just a grand way to point at the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramel is a soft toffee made from sugar and butter, a chewy confection.

clue.text: Attractive person, dear to the French, seizing power

indicators.note: to seize is to grab and hold, so one piece takes hold of another

blocks.note: cher is French for dear
arm as in the strong arm of the law, force

explanation.surface: A handsome figure, beloved by the French, grabs control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dear to the French' reads as popular in France; it is a translation of the word 'dear'.
explanation.definitionFit: A charmer is someone who is pleasing and delightful, who wins people over easily.

clue.text: Note Clio, for example, departs, seeing the funny side

blocks.note: A is a musical note
Clio is the Greek Muse of history
the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A message saying the woman called Clio has left, and someone finds it comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for example' tells you Clio is one instance of a class: she is one of the nine Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amused finds something funny, which is the state of appreciating the joke.

clue.text: Muslim lawyer’s everyday clothing

blocks.note: first meaning: a scholar who gives rulings on Islamic law
second meaning: civilian dress worn by someone usually in uniform

explanation.surface: What a Muslim legal expert wears day to day.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is 'is', joining two unrelated meanings of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an Islamic jurist who issues fatwas and plain civilian dress worn off duty.

clue.text: Sailor’s right to lead managers

blocks.note: to star in a film is to take the lead role
a company's board of directors manages it

explanation.surface: A seaman is entitled to be in charge of the executives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right to lead' reads as an entitlement; 'right' belongs to the definition and 'to lead' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, starboard is the right-hand side when facing forward, the nautical term for right.

clue.text: Wake-up call in the style of the jollies?

blocks.note: from the French à la, in the manner of
the Royal Marines, nicknamed the Jollies

explanation.surface: A morning call done the way cheerful holidaymakers do it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jollies' suggests fun outings; it is the old slang name for the Royal Marines, abbreviated RM.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a signal or device that rouses a sleeper, a literal call to wake up.

clue.text: Ruse devised by informer in theatre musical to begin with

indicators.note: one thing placed within another sits inside it
what comes to begin with is the opening letter

blocks.note: the stage stands for the theatre
a rat is someone who informs on others
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A scheme cooked up by a grass inside a theatre show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre musical' reads as one phrase, a stage show, but the words split between two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning plan to deceive or outwit, which is a ruse.

clue.text: Old wash round ears at first, and go

indicators.note: to go round something is to enclose it
at first points to the opening letter

blocks.note: lave is an archaic word for wash
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Wash behind your ears first, then head off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' marks the word as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a place is to depart from it, and 'go' is an everyday synonym.

clue.text: Chaperon about to arrive — retired woman

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw, to go back, so letters run backwards

blocks.note: a train that is due is expected soon
any woman's name can stand for a woman

explanation.surface: A chaperone is due any minute; she is a pensioner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired woman' suggests a pensioner; the adjective actually tells you to turn her name round.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman who acts as governess and companion to young girls in a Spanish family.

clue.text: National flag originally hoisted by crew

indicators.note: originally points to the start of a word, its first letter
by means beside, so the next piece is placed alongside

blocks.note: the yellow flag is a wild iris
the opening letter of the word
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: A country's flag is first raised by the crew of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National flag' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'National', a citizen, and the flag is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a particular country, and an Irishman is one such citizen of Ireland.
